title: Esports Performance, Coaching & Psychology Atlas
description: Curriculum-first concept map for Pearson BTEC Level 3 Esports Units 2, 4, 12 and 13, linking performance analysis, practice, coaching, wellbeing and psychology.

curriculumPresets.title: Full performance system
curriculumPresets.description: Explore how analysis, practice, coaching, psychology and wellbeing combine to influence competitive performance.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 2: Skills, Strategies and Analysis
curriculumPresets.description: Follow mechanics, tactics, strategy, communication, VOD review and performance indicators from observation to adaptation.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 4: Health, Wellbeing and Fitness
curriculumPresets.description: Connect physical preparation, ergonomics, recovery, sleep and wellbeing to sustainable esports performance.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 12: Coaching
curriculumPresets.description: Trace needs analysis through goal setting, practice design, observation, feedback and reassessment.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 13: Psychology
curriculumPresets.description: Explore motivation, confidence, attention, arousal, anxiety, cohesion and psychological skills training.

nodes.name: Esports Performance System
nodes.note: Competitive performance emerges from interacting technical, tactical, psychological, physical and social factors.
nodes.hook: Choose one recent match and classify every cause of success or failure into this system.

nodes.name: Performance Analysis
nodes.note: Analysis turns observations and data into evidence about current performance.
nodes.hook: Separate description from analysis: what happened, why did it happen, and what should change?

nodes.name: Mechanical Skill
nodes.note: Mechanical skill covers execution such as aim, movement, inputs, timing and ability use.
nodes.hook: Identify one measurable mechanical skill in your chosen title and define a repeatable test for it.

nodes.name: Tactics
nodes.note: Tactics are short- to medium-term choices used to gain advantage within a match.
nodes.hook: Find a tactical decision that only makes sense because of the current game state.

nodes.name: Strategy
nodes.note: Strategy sets the broader approach a player or team intends to use across a map, round, match or series.
nodes.hook: Explain the difference between one strategy and one tactic from the same match.

nodes.name: Game Sense & Decision Making
nodes.note: Game sense combines awareness, prediction, information and judgement under time pressure.
nodes.hook: Pause a VOD before a decision and list the information available to the player at that exact moment.

nodes.name: Team Communication
nodes.note: Effective communication transfers relevant information quickly, accurately and with suitable priority.
nodes.hook: Rewrite three overloaded comms into short callouts that preserve the important information.

nodes.name: VOD Review
nodes.note: Recorded match review allows decisions, positioning, timing and team interactions to be inspected after play.
nodes.hook: Create a timestamp log with evidence, interpretation and action columns.

nodes.name: Performance Indicators
nodes.note: Indicators are selected measures used to track aspects of performance; useful measures depend on game, role and objective.
nodes.hook: Pick three indicators and explain why a high value is not automatically good performance.

nodes.name: Practice & Skill Development
nodes.note: Practice should target a diagnosed need and provide enough repetition, challenge and feedback to cause adaptation.
nodes.hook: Turn one weakness from a VOD review into a 30-minute practice block.

nodes.name: Deliberate Practice
nodes.note: Deliberate practice is focused practice with a clear target, suitable difficulty and feedback rather than repetition without reflection.
nodes.hook: Compare playing ranked for an hour with a deliberately designed practice task.

nodes.name: Drills
nodes.note: Drills isolate or constrain a skill so it can be repeated and improved efficiently.
nodes.hook: Design a drill, then state what transfer you expect back into real matches.

nodes.name: Scrimmage Practice
nodes.note: Scrims provide representative team practice against opposition while allowing planned experimentation and review.
nodes.hook: Define what evidence would make a scrim useful even if your team loses it.

nodes.name: Feedback Loop
nodes.note: Performance improves through a repeated cycle of action, observation, feedback, adjustment and retesting.
nodes.hook: Draw one complete feedback loop using evidence from an actual player.

nodes.name: Coaching Process
nodes.note: Coaching structures diagnosis, goal setting, intervention, observation and evaluation around the needs of a player or team.
nodes.hook: Audit a coaching plan: which stage is weakest and what evidence is missing?

nodes.name: Needs Analysis
nodes.note: Needs analysis identifies the gap between current and desired performance using appropriate evidence.
nodes.hook: Triangulate one need using observation, player self-report and a performance measure.

nodes.name: Goal Setting
nodes.note: Goals give direction to practice and evaluation when they are specific enough to guide action and review.
nodes.hook: Convert a vague goal such as improve aim into an evidence-based performance goal.

nodes.name: Coaching Intervention
nodes.note: An intervention is a planned change to practice, behaviour, communication or preparation intended to improve a diagnosed need.
nodes.hook: Explain why the same intervention might work for one player and fail for another.

nodes.name: Coach Feedback
nodes.note: Feedback should be timely, evidence-based and matched to the learner's needs and ability to act on it.
nodes.hook: Rewrite judgemental feedback into observable evidence plus a next action.

nodes.name: Performance Psychology
nodes.note: Psychological factors influence attention, confidence, motivation, communication and decision making during preparation and competition.
nodes.hook: Choose a performance problem and argue whether its main cause is psychological, tactical or environmental.

nodes.name: Motivation
nodes.note: Motivation affects effort, persistence and willingness to engage with practice or competition.
nodes.hook: Distinguish an intrinsic and extrinsic motivator for the same player.

nodes.name: Confidence
nodes.note: Confidence shapes expectations and willingness to execute decisions, but overconfidence can also reduce judgement quality.
nodes.hook: Find evidence that distinguishes confidence from simply winning recently.

nodes.name: Attention & Focus
nodes.note: Attention determines which information is selected and maintained when many visual, auditory and tactical cues compete for processing.
nodes.hook: List the cues a player must ignore as well as the cues they must notice.

nodes.name: Arousal
nodes.note: Arousal describes activation level; too little or too much can interfere with performance depending on the task and person.
nodes.hook: Explain why the ideal activation level may differ between an aim duel and an IGL decision.

nodes.name: Competitive Anxiety
nodes.note: Anxiety can alter attention, confidence, physical state and decision making before or during competition.
nodes.hook: Separate observable signs of anxiety from assumptions about what a player feels.

nodes.name: Team Cohesion
nodes.note: Cohesion concerns how effectively a group stays connected around task and social goals.
nodes.hook: Identify one team behaviour that indicates task cohesion rather than friendship.

nodes.name: Psychological Skills Training
nodes.note: Psychological skills training deliberately practises techniques such as routines, self-talk, imagery, breathing and goal setting.
nodes.hook: Match one technique to a specific performance problem and justify the choice.

nodes.name: Health, Wellbeing & Fitness
nodes.note: Sustainable esports performance depends on managing physical activity, recovery, ergonomics, sleep and mental wellbeing.
nodes.hook: Audit a weekly esports routine for risks that could reduce performance or health.

nodes.name: Ergonomics & DSE
nodes.note: Workstation setup, posture, input-device use and breaks influence comfort and musculoskeletal risk during prolonged screen work.
nodes.hook: Use HSE guidance to critique a real esports workstation rather than relying on gaming-chair marketing.

nodes.name: Physical Activity
nodes.note: Regular physical activity supports general health and counters some risks associated with prolonged sedentary behaviour.
nodes.hook: Build a realistic activity plan around an esports timetable without pretending gym work directly replaces game practice.

nodes.name: Sleep & Recovery
nodes.note: Recovery practices influence readiness, attention and consistency across repeated training and competition sessions.
nodes.hook: Identify which parts of a tournament schedule make good recovery hardest and propose controls.
